articles.title: Metal PCB and PCBA Manufacturing: A Practical Guide to Materials, Assembly, and Global Sourcing
articles.excerpt: As electronic products become more compact and powerful, manufacturers face a growing challenge: how to manage heat while maintaining reliable electrical performance. This is particularly important in…
articles.body: As electronic products become more compact and powerful, manufacturers face a growing challenge: how to manage heat while maintaining reliable electrical performance. This is particularly important in LED lighting, industrial electronics, automotive systems, and power conversion equipment, where components can generate significant heat during operation. Metal printed circuit boards (metal PCBs) provide one approach to this challenge. By incorporating a metal base into the board structure, they can help transfer heat away from critical components. When these boards move into production, printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) introduces another set of considerations, including component sourcing, soldering, inspection, and functional testing.

articles.title: Cloud Pub/Sub Dead-Letter Recovery for Node.js Weekly Support Digests
articles.excerpt: Cloud Pub/Sub Dead-Letter Recovery for Node.js Weekly Support Digests Short answer: for Google Cloud Pub/Sub dead-letter retries versus an AWS SQS DLQ, choose the queue whose retention, delivery attem…
articles.body: Cloud Pub/Sub Dead-Letter Recovery for Node.js Weekly Support Digests Short answer: for Google Cloud Pub/Sub dead-letter retries versus an AWS SQS DLQ, choose the queue whose retention, delivery attempts, and replay permissions fit the weekly deadline, then keep idempotency and failure classification in the Node.js worker. Start with the recovery window. Recovery needs a clock. That window is the time between a failed active-customer digest and the point where the support team can no longer send it usefully. If the weekly report is due Monday morning, a queue that retains a dead-letter message is only part of the answer. The application must preserve the digest identity, record the attempt classification, and expose enough context for a replay decision.

articles.title: How to Autofill PDF Forms with AI
articles.excerpt: I've spent the last few months building an AI tool that fills PDF forms from a user's own documents (a passport, a W-2, a spreadsheet, or just a few typed sentences). The first version was the obvious…
articles.body: I've spent the last few months building an AI tool that fills PDF forms from a user's own documents (a passport, a W-2, a spreadsheet, or just a few typed sentences). The first version was the obvious one: send the PDF to an LLM and ask it to fill the form. It didn't work. This post covers what did work, with code, so you can build your own. Full disclosure: the tool is Simplifier . Everything below works with any stack and any LLM. The core idea: split "understanding" from "doing" LLMs are great at understanding meaning : "this passport says the date of birth is 03/14/1990, and this form field asks for DOB." They're bad at precise, mechanical work: exact field names, coordinates, checkbox export values. So the pipeline looks like this: Code reads the form's fields.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent 27 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23), in its first Starlink launch in 11 days.
articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.

articles.excerpt: NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight, which is scheduled to launch to Earth orbit next year. But a firm liftoff date has not yet been announced.
articles.body: NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight. The agency laid out a detailed concept of operations for Artemis III today (Oct. 23) during a press conference at Kennedy Space Center , stressing how important the flight is to its moon plans and how challenging it will be to make everything go right. "We're launching three of the most powerful rockets in the world, and undertaking what is likely the most complicated launch campaign ever undertaken," Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, said during today's event, which lasted more than two hours.
